domain: Takes a single owner id (r0). Calls the veneer at 0x08077008 (OwnerState_GetFar / Func_08077008, already declared in owner_state.h returning struct OwnerInventoryState*) and scans its inventory[15] u16 array (offset 0xd8/216, matching owner_state.h's existing LAYOUT_OFFSET_GUARD) from slot 0 upward. For each encoded slot value: if it is 0, the scan stops and the function returns 1 (empty/terminator reached). If bit 0x200 is set (an 'equipped' flag, consistent with the sibling get_item_quantity.c's item-slot bit layout: 0x1FF item id, bits 11-15 quantity-1), the slot is skipped and the scan continues (up to 15 slots; exhausting all 15 without a hit returns 0). Otherwise -- the first present, non-equipped slot found -- it computes quantity = ((encoded>>11)!=0) ? (encoded>>11)+1 : 1, then calls the veneer at 0x08077058 (which itself long-jumps to 0x080788c4 = Inventory_Remove(owner,slot) per inventory.h) exactly `quantity` times with (owner_id, slot), and returns 1 if the LAST call's return value was 2, else 0. Net effect: finds the first non-equipped item stack and removes it unit-by-unit (fully emptying that slot), reporting success (1) only if the final removal call signalled 2.
notes: The family-matcher's best guess, games/gs1/src/battle/summon/reset_charge.c (score 7342/10000, below the 7500 threshold), is a false positive: it has no relation to this owner's actual semantics (different registers, different callees, no inventory-slot bit logic). Real evidence instead: this owner's address (0x080a40ac) sits in a solid run of already-adopted inventory_menu/*.c owners in source-paths.json -- immediately preceded by main:080a3e88 (inventory_menu/refresh_owner_items.c) and immediately followed, byte-exact (0x080a40ac + 100 = 0x080a4110), by main:080a4110 (inventory_menu/get_command_cursor_x.c). Its first callee (bl to the veneer at 0x08077008) is already declared in owner_state.h as `struct OwnerInventoryState *Func_08077008(s32 owner)` / `#define OwnerState_GetFar Func_08077008`, and the 216-byte (0xd8) offset it reads matches that header's own `LAYOUT_OFFSET_GUARD(OwnerInventoryState_Inventory, ..., inventory, 0x0d8)` exactly. Its second callee (bl to the veneer at 0x08077058) resolves (per the veneer's own retained .4byte target, 0x080788c5 with the Thumb bit stripped -> 0x080788c4) to Func_080788c4, which inventory.h already names `Inventory_Remove` -- so this owner is a genuine, already-connected member of the inventory subsystem, not the battle/summon family the template suggested.

Cloned m2c (matt-kempster/m2c) and ran `compiler workbench` (temporarily registering a placeholder name to satisfy the tool, removed again afterward since exact adoption was not reached) to get an m2c-informed structural hypothesis using the project's real agscc type context. m2c's decompiled output independently reproduced the same control flow this draft had already derived by hand (same terminator/equipped-skip/removal-loop/shared-return-1-tail shape), which increases confidence in the recovered algorithm even though the byte-level match remains incomplete.

Iterated roughly a dozen structurally distinct hand-drafts (do-while vs while vs for for the inner removal loop; a guarded vs unguarded removal loop; encoded read merged into the while-condition vs split into a separate prefetch/test variable matching the reference's redundant reload; struct-field indexing vs a cached u16* pointer; a single `return` vs a goto-unified single-exit tail with a dedicated carry variable copied to the return register, matching the reference's `adds r1,r0,#0` / `adds r0,r1,#0` pattern) without applying any register hint, asm(), or hand scheduling -- only ordinary, plausible C shapes. Best result: 92/100 candidate bytes, 33 differing halfwords, 36 wrong instructions (down from an initial naive draft's 94 bytes / 43 differing halfwords / 49 wrong instructions).

Residual gap is concentrated in one persistent, small structural knot: the reference's prologue loads the 216 struct offset into a register for a register-offset ldrh (`movs r3,#216; ldrh r3,[r0,r3]`) as a one-off PRE-loop test read, then separately bumps the pointer by an immediate 216 for the walking body reads, and shares that pre-test with the loop-back edge via an unconditional jump to a bottom test (`b.n .L0`) rather than an immediate top-of-loop compare+branch; it also loads the 0x200 equip-bit mask from an inline literal pool (`ldr r3,[pc,#40]` -> `.4byte 0x00000200`, placed as dead data right after an already-required branch) instead of synthesizing it with movs+lsls. Every natural source rewrite tried either reproduced the compiler's own (smaller, correct-behavior) synthesis of 0x200 and an immediate top test, or, when forced toward the reference's exact prefetch/shared-test shape via genuinely different source (a manual goto-based rotated loop, or splitting the test read from the body read), lost the compiler's loop-strength-reduction (address recomputed via `lsls+ldrh[r,r]` per iteration instead of a walked pointer) and got further from the reference, or required extra live-range pressure that spilled a variable to r8 (mov r7,r8; push {r7}) rather than reusing r1/r5 the way the reference does. This reads as a genuine small, persistent compiler-scheduling/allocation difference (per Cleanroom's 'invert a stalled last mile' guidance) rather than a wrong overall model -- the algorithm, callees, offsets, and loop trip count are all corroborated by two independent methods (hand trace + m2c) and match the header-declared struct layout exactly.

rejected_experiments.result: compiled to `asrs` (arithmetic shift) instead of the reference's `lsrs` (logical shift) -- same numeric result for this value range but a different opcode/byte pattern. Fixed by shifting through `(u32)encoded >> 11` while keeping `encoded` itself as a plain s32 (a u16-typed local instead produced spurious lsls/asrs #16 sign-extension shuffles on every use).
